title: Dynamic KV Watermarks and Compaction Scheduling to Reduce GPU Memory Fragmentation
creator: Priya Shah
description: Problem: As continuous batching and long-running inference workloads increase, the KV cache on GPUs exhibits progressive internal fragmentation. Small, variable-length KV entries combined with variable batch sequence lengths cause allocation hotspots and unusable gaps, increasing OOM events and leading to unnecessary offloading or quantization. Goal: Introduce an allocation strategy driven by live telemetry (watermarks per pool), cooperative compaction scheduling, and allocation segregation (hot/cold) to reduce fragmentation while preserving latency SLOs. This ticket scopes the design, prototype allocator changes, scheduling heuristics, and rollout plan for runtime-1.20.
motivation_and_goals: Reduce fragmentation-induced OOMs by 40% on 8xA100 pools for typical chat workloads; avoid adding tail latency > 5ms P95; enable greedy background compaction windows that are batching-aware and cost-accounted to customer usage buckets.
constraints: Must be compatible with existing KV eviction APIs, not require model changes, and work with private and dedicated deployments. Changes should be togglable via runtime flag and observable in Console dashboards.
design_notes: 1) Introduce dynamic watermarks per KV pool: low/soft/high expressed in bytes and in fraction of pool. 2) On allocation, prefer slab/slot classes favoring placement into pools below soft watermark; if allocation would push above high watermark, trigger placement fallback and possible preemptive relocation. 3) Track allocation lifetimes and heat score to label blocks hot (frequently accessed KV) or cold (rare). Cold blocks will be preferred for background compaction moves. 4) Compaction scheduler runs cooperative relocations during identified batching lull windows: uses batching telemetry to avoid interfering with live request paths. 5) Make compaction incremental and bounded per cycle to limit tail latency. 6) Expose new telemetry: fragmentation ratio, largest free region size, relocations/sec, compaction window utilization.
tradeoffs_considered: - Aggressive compaction reduces fragmentation but risks P95 latency spikes; we limit relocation quantum per compaction tick. - Larger slot coarse-grained allocation reduces fragmentation but increases internal waste for small KVs. We adopt hot/cold segregation to balance this. - Background compaction consumes GPU bandwidth; we throttle based on current GPU utilization and batching forecast.
implementation_plan: Add per-pool watermark config and runtime flags
Implement allocation policy that consults watermarks and heat scores
Implement heat scoring module using access counters + decay
Build compaction scheduler that subscribes to batching telemetry and GPU util metrics
Wire new telemetry to Console and add dashboards + alerts
Add unit + integration tests and synthetic workloads
Roll out behind feature flag and run canary on dedicated pools
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic chat workload shows >= 40% reduction in fragmentation metric vs baseline for 90th percentile sequence lengths
No regression in P50/P95 generation latency beyond 5ms for canary traffic
Compaction activity is observed only during identified low-batch windows in telemetry
Feature flag allows safe rollback without state corruption
Console shows new panels for fragmentation and relocation costs
test_plan: Unit-tests for allocator decision logic and watermark thresholds
Integration test: run continuous-batching simulator with mixed sequence lengths and verify memory map and fragmentation metrics
Load test: run canary on 8xA100 dedicated pool for 48h comparing OOMs and offload events
Chaos test: kill compaction worker process and ensure allocations still succeed and no data loss
rollout_plan: Merge behind feature flag and land initial PR to canary branch
Deploy to internal staging with telemetry dashboards and alerts
Enable on 2 small dedicated pools for 72h, monitor fragmentation and latency
Gradually enable for 10% of hosted traffic with opt-in via account flag
Full enable when metrics stable for 7 days
